_comment: Baked Node.js end-of-life table, consumed by scripts/check-runtime-node-eol.mjs. BAKED, NOT FETCHED, deliberately: the gate must be able to DECIDE without the network, so a CI runner with no egress fails on a real EOL rather than on a fetch timeout. Placed under scripts/data/ (alongside cloudflare-ip-ranges.json) and NOT under audits/, which Dockerfile:13 COPYs as a Stage-1 build input that projects into the PUBLIC knowledge bundle.
_source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/Release/main/schedule.json — the official nodejs/Release SoT. Values below were read from it on the probe date, not from memory.
_how_to_refresh: curl the source above and re-copy the `end` dates for every major listed here, then move revisit_by forward. A major that disappears upstream should be KEPT here with its historical EOL date — an old Dockerfile pinned to it must still fail.
_revisit_rationale: Node 26 enters LTS 2026-10-28 and Node 28 is announced around 2027-04; refreshing each January keeps this table ahead of both. If it is stale past revisit_by the canary reports INDETERMINATE (exit 3) rather than silently trusting an aging table — a defensive threshold that expires, per the CLAUDE.md defensive-threshold discipline.
_warning_window_rationale: A major inside its last 90 days is reported as a WARNING (still exit 0) so a bump can be scheduled deliberately; past EOL is a hard FAIL. 90 days is roughly one release train — enough to plan a runtime bump without an emergency.
